call_points.text: CGFMU claims of ₹450-550 Cr across three cohorts in FY27; first claim timing Q1 or Q2.
CGFMU claims cut headline GNPA but are unlikely to affect P&L.
Cost of funds has hardened; elevated Q4 rates have not fallen as usual, with a rush for deposits among SFBs.
A diesel price rise above 10-15% could hit the commercial vehicle book; no impact seen yet.
RoA path starts at 1.2% in Q1 and rises to 1.6% by Q4FY27.
Inclusive finance book targeted at ~₹7,500 Cr, up 25% YoY and 45% of the total book, on a shift to individual Vikas loans.
Retail assets guided to +45% YoY, with CV book ~₹2,800 Cr (+55%) and mortgage ~₹4,200 Cr (+45%).
100 new branches planned in FY27 to deepen micro-banking penetration.
Digital deposits and credit line on UPI each targeted to roughly double in FY27.

penalties.authority: Reserve Bank of India – Integrated Ombudsman (Office of RBI Ombudsman, Raipur)
penalties.details: Award passed under Clause 15(1)(b) of the Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 vide Award dated January 05, 2026, directing the Bank to (i) waive/refund foreclosure charges of ₹16,00,000 plus applicable GST, (ii) pay compensation of ₹50,000 to the complainant, and (iii) issue No Dues Certificate and correct credit bureau records, if impacted. Further to the earlier disclosure made by the Bank, the Bank had appeal the matter to the Appellate Authority wherein vide order dated May 15, 2026, the Appellate Authority upheld the Award and additionally directed the Bank to pay interest on the foreclosure charges at the Bank Rate (5.5%) from the date of deduction till the date of refund.
penalties.impact: Financial impact includes waiver/refund of foreclosure charges amounting to ₹16,00,000 plus applicable GST, payment of compensation of ₹50,000 to the complainant, and payment of interest on the foreclosure charges at the Bank Rate (5.5%) from the date of deduction till the date of refund. No material impact on the Bank's operations or overall financial position.

operating_notes.text: Gross NPAs were ₹86,418 lakh (6.55% of gross advances) and net NPAs ₹54,188 lakh (4.21%) at March 31, 2026.

The Bank transferred loans not in default with aggregate principal outstanding of ₹13,66,184 lakh for consideration of ₹12,978.75 lakh under RBI's SFB Transfer and Distribution of Credit Risk Directions, 2025.
Floating provision stood at ₹5,917 lakh as on March 31, 2026, of which ₹2,210 lakh was created during the year.
Slippages fell from ₹264 Cr in Q4FY25 to ₹116 Cr in Q3FY26 and ₹74 Cr in Q4FY26.
As of Mar-26, ₹508 Cr of the ₹541.9 Cr NNPA is receivable under CGFMU cohorts.
Digital deposits were ₹1,672 Cr, 12% of the liability book, with a ~₹6 Cr/day sourcing run rate.
FY26 deposits ₹13,994 Cr, up 32.3% YoY; CASA ratio 22.6%; retail deposits 86% of the book.
Commercial vehicle book ₹1,819 Cr (+36% YoY) and mortgage book ₹3,013 Cr (+38% YoY) at Mar-2026.
Credit on UPI outstanding about ₹200 Cr at the end of the billing cycle, with 90+ delinquency around 1.5%.
Board approved issuance of up to ₹100 Cr of Lower Tier II Non-Convertible Debentures on a private placement basis.
